newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Matthews to open new UK PR firm in April.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Matthews to open new UK PR firm in April.

text.p: Chris Matthews, former Shandwick Consultants chief executive, said on Tuesday he planned to open a new PR company on April 1.
Matthews is setting up the Hogarth Partnership with three other Shandwick Consultant directors and an associate director who are all leaving the firm, part of Shandwick International Plc.
Mathews said that the new company would aim to serve the growing number of major companies who now have their own inhouse PR teams, helping out on specific projects.
"They tend to need help in two sets of circumstances, firstly if there is a crisis and secondly to help them think about longer-term issues," he said.
Matthews said that the major consultancies have not adapted to the fact that so many major companies do their own PR.
He said that the new firm would ultimately aim at serving major FTSE-100 clients but added: "In the first couple of years if it moves we'll do PR for it."
He said the company planned to have an initial staff of around 10 people, increasing to no more than 50 over time.
Matthews and fellow Shandwick departees John Olsen, Rachel Hirst, Nick Denton and James Longfield have raised an intial 200,000 pounds to fund the company.
But Matthews said initial cash flow projections indicated that only 50,000 pounds would be needed to get the company up and running.
